name: La Réserve Eden au Lac Zurich
positioning: Lakeside hotel in Zurich, the former Eden au Lac, redesigned by Philippe Starck for La Réserve, with a sixth-floor Japanese-Peruvian restaurant under the dome and a Mediterranean-Italian kitchen on the ground floor
best_for: Design lovers who want Philippe Starck's take on a historic lakeside hotel
Food and cocktail lovers who want two distinct restaurants and a bar with a full mocktail menu in the hotel
Summer visitors who want the Utoquai lake bathing area right in front of the hotel

facts.text: Philippe Starck redesigned the hotel for La Réserve.
The Eden au Lac has been a Zurich institution since 1909.
The larger lake-facing rooms have balconies with views of the Alps.
La Muña serves Japanese-Peruvian dishes for sharing.
La Muña has a 360-degree view of the historic center, with the lake and the Alps in the distance.
La Muña's indoor room occupies the former attic beneath the hotel's dome.
Stained-glass windows by Ara Starck guide the light through the dome.
Eden Kitchen and Bar is on the ground floor, with large bay windows opening onto the outside.
Eden Kitchen's menu draws on Mediterranean-Italian culinary traditions.
Marco Ortolani is the Italian executive chef at Eden Kitchen.
DJs play at the Eden Bar in the evening.
Conde Nast Traveler describes a small fumoir off to one side of the ground floor, behind an unmarked door.

highlights.text: Philippe Starck says the design was inspired by an imaginary yacht club.
Skiffs and kayaks are mounted vertically inside the dome as a sculpture.
La Muña is on the sixth floor, reached by a glass elevator from the lobby, with a tree-lined roof terrace.
The Eden Bar menu is divided equally between cocktails and mocktails.
The Utoquai bathing area on Lake Zurich is just in front of the hotel.

considerations.text: The rooftop bar opens only in summer.
Arrival by car is via Kreuzstrasse, where the hotel's main entrance is.
WhataHotel notes limited parking in the central location.
